reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Commission creation, policies, fund allocation, and state representation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1943 p. 839 § 3, A.L. 1961 p. 31, A.L. 1980 S.B. 612, A.L. 1986 H.B. 1172, A.L. 1995 S.B. 3, S.B. 65, A.L. 2000 S.B. 741, A.L. 2001 S.B. 462). Establishes the State Soil and Water Districts Commission to administer sections 278.060 to 278.300, formulate policies/programs, allocate appropriated funds including a cost-share program, convey state aid (except locally raised district aid administered by the district governing body), and represent the state. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Commission membership, geographic balance, qualifications, and terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Sets composition at four ex officio members and six governor-appointed, senate-confirmed farmer members (three north and three south of the Missouri River, max one per senatorial district, max four from one political party, farm title/principal livelihood qualifications, unlimited three-year terms, June 27, 2000 holdover transition, vacancy appointments, and holdover service). Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Attorney general legal services for the commission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes the state soil and water districts commission to call upon the attorney general for required legal services. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Officers, voting, quorum, expenses, bonds, records, and audits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Governs annual chairman and vice chairman selection, nonvoting ex officio members, four-farmer-member quorum with three-member concurrence at a four-member meeting, farmer-member expenses, officer/employee surety bonds, proceeding/order records, and annual account audits. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Enumerated commission powers, federal-state aid, and cost-share rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 including subdivisions (1)-(9) and history note. Lists nine powers and duties covering district formation, referendum/supervisor rules, section 278.100 petitions/hearings/referendums, program advice, training/assistance, federal/state cooperation, federal/state aid determinations and withholding (noting verbatim repeated clause "to advise any soil and water conservation district;" in subdivision (7)), general assistance, and chapter 536 cost-share rulemaking. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified subdivisions (1)-(9) including verbatim repeated phrase "to advise any soil and water conservation district;" in subdivision (7) and chapter 536 cost-share rulemaking in (9).

headings.title: Individual rule variances and administrative rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Permits individual variances from rules or regulations unless prohibited by federal or state law upon adequate proof that compliance with sections 278.070 to 278.300 (archived range begins at 278.070 here) or commission requirements has an arbitrary and unreasonable impact on participating landowners, and directs rulemaking and guidelines. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified archived citation range "sections 278.070 to 278.300" (beginning at 278.070 here versus 278.060 in subsections 1 and 5) and federal/state law qualification.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–6 (including subdivisions (1)–(9) of sub 5) and history note (through 2001 S.B. 462); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed commission creation under sections 278.060 to 278.300, local-aid exception, 4 ex officio + 6 farmer members with June 27, 2000 holdover transition, attorney general counsel, quorum/voting/audit rules, verbatim repeated clause in sub 5(7), chapter 536 cost-share rulemaking, and individual variances citing archived range "sections 278.070 to 278.300" (beginning at 278.070 rather than 278.060). All 6 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: District formation petition, public hearing, survey, and referendum
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1943 p. 839 § 4, A.L. 1961 p. 31). Sets signature thresholds for county or township establishment petitions (25 land representatives per township or 50% if fewer than 50), commission validity review, local public hearing, farmland survey of necessity and administrative feasibility, and ballot referendum of area land representatives. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Referendum outcome, two-year waiting period, and township additions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1943 p. 839 § 4, A.L. 1961 p. 31). Directs declaring a district established upon majority approval and substantial expression of opinion, bars another referendum for two years after defeat (conditioned on evidence of more general desire), and permits adding other townships in the same county by the same procedure. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised "reapplication limit" to "two-year waiting period" to match the statutory rule on calling another referendum after defeat. (Prior draft: "Referendum declaration, two-year reapplication limit, and township additions".)

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (through 1961 p. 31); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed township signature thresholds (25 or 50% if under 50), hearing, farmland survey, ballot referendum, majority + substantial-expression establishment rule, 2-year wait before another referendum upon evidence of more general desire, and same-county township additions. Revised sub 2 title to "two-year waiting period" for precision; retained sub 1.

headings.title: District supervisor board composition and election rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1943 p. 839 § 5, A.L. 1961 p. 31, A.L. 1980 S.B. 612). Directs the commission after district establishment under section 278.100 to arrange a five-member local governing board comprising the ex officio county agricultural extension agent and four elected resident taxpaying land representatives, prohibiting elections on regular county political election dates. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Supervisor terms, staggered elections, vacancies, and reelection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Sets coincident term for the ex officio member, four-year terms for elected supervisors with staggered two- and four-year transitions keyed to October 13, 1961, commission appointment of resident land representative successors for vacancies, and reelection eligibility. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Board quorum, majority concurrence, and officers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Establishes a majority quorum while requiring concurrence of a majority of the whole board for determinations, directs electing a chairman from the board, and designates the county agricultural extension agent as secretary. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Supervisor expense reimbursement and district staff employment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Provides no compensation for supervisors other than necessary expenses including travel, and authorizes the board to employ assistants within available funds and set their qualifications, compensation, and duties. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Submitting district documents for approval and activity information
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires the board of supervisors to submit contemplated rules, regulations, forms, and other documents to the state commission for approval, plus other requested activity information. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised title to highlight that contemplated district rules, forms, and documents are submitted for commission approval. (Prior draft: "Submission of district documents and information to commission".)

headings.title: Surety bonds, board records, and annual audit statements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires executing surety bonds for officers and employees entrusted with funds or property, keeping full records of proceedings, resolutions, and regulations, and presenting an annual audit statement to the state commission for approval. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Advisory consultation with nearby municipalities and counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Permits the board of supervisors to invite nearby municipal or county legislative bodies to designate an advisory representative on program and policy questions affecting their property, water supply, or other interests. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Cost-share administration and recordable landowner agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 including subdivisions (1)-(2) and history note. Directs supervisors to assist the commission in administering a state cost-share program and authorizes recordable landowner agreements stipulating ten-year/expected-life refund duties for altered or removed projects and maintenance duties with potential access easements in undue-hardship cases (noting singular "soil and water district commission" in subdivision (2)). Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified subdivisions (1)-(2) including archived singular "soil and water district commission" in subdivision (2).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–8 (including subdivisions (1)–(2) of sub 8) and history note (through 1980 S.B. 612); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed 5-member board under section 278.100, non-political election date, October 13, 1961 staggered terms, whole-board majority concurrence, expense-only service, document approval submissions, surety bonds/audits, municipal/county advisory consultation, and recordable cost-share agreements (noting archived singular "soil and water district commission" in sub 8(2)). Revised sub 5 title to capture commission approval; retained subs 1–4 and 6–8.

headings.title: Corporate status, debt and lien limits, and official title
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1943 p. 839 § 6, A.L. 1961 p. 31). Declares organized soil and water districts bodies corporate with limited powers, exempts private property and land representatives from district debts and non-district property from liens, sets the county-commission-designated official title, and grants capacity to sue, be sued, and contract. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: District powers, voluntary landowner consent, and federal-private aid
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)-(6) and history note. Lists six powers and duties of districts through their supervisors: promoting conservation measures aligned with the University of Missouri college of agriculture, cooperating with agencies and land representatives (barring on-farm programs without full landowner consent), furnishing services/materials/equipment, accepting federal grants, executing commission-approved contracts, and accepting other contributions with wastage-prevention agreements. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 (including subdivisions (1)–(6) of sub 2) and history note (through 1961 p. 31); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed limited corporate status, private-property debt/lien exemptions, county-commission official title, MU college of agriculture alignment, mandatory full landowner consent for on-farm programs, federal/other contributions, and commission-approved contracts. Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Prohibited and restricted powers of district supervisors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)-(8) and history/effective-date notes (L. 1943 p. 839 § 7, A.L. 1961 p. 31, A.L. 1965 p. 95, A.L. 2000 S.B. 741; effective 6-27-00). Prohibits district supervisors from exercising eminent domain, incurring indebtedness beyond available funds, issuing bonds, levying taxes or assessments, exacting contributions, marketing/buying/selling non-conservation farm products or supplies (subject to section 278.135), or conducting agricultural research/extension teaching except under Missouri college of agriculture instruction. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised title to acknowledge the qualified carveouts in subdivisions (7) (conservation supplies subject to section 278.135) and (8) (college of agriculture instruction). (Prior draft: "Prohibited powers and activities of district supervisors".)

headings.title: Acceptance of voluntary conservation donations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes. Permits supervisors to accept voluntary contributions from any source solely to promote soil and water saving within the district if donors are satisfactorily guaranteed faithful use for that purpose. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 (including subdivisions (1)–(8) of sub 1) and history/effective-date notes (effective 6-27-00); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed prohibitions on eminent domain, excess debt, bonds, taxes, assessments, and exacted contributions, qualified restrictions on conservation supplies (subject to section 278.135) and agricultural research/extension (MU college of agriculture instruction), and voluntary conservation donations. Revised sub 1 title to acknowledge restricted/qualified powers alongside flat prohibitions; retained sub 2.

headings.title: Three-complaint approval trigger and complaint-procedure notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 2000 S.B. 741; effective 6-27-00). Requires a district marketing or buying and selling soil-conservation farm products to obtain commission approval to continue if three or more business entities submit written complaints, and requires all districts upon request to provide complaint-procedure and commission contact information. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised title to cover both the three-business-complaint approval trigger and the mandatory disclosure of complaint procedures upon any person's request. (Prior draft: "Commission approval trigger after three business complaints".)

headings.title: Complaint review, approval criteria, and subsequent complaint bars
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)-(2) and continuation text in subdivision (2), plus history/effective-date notes. Directs commission notice and a 60-day district information request, requires considering public and business comments, limits approval to products reasonably related to soil and water conservation and not readily available in the area, and bars new complaints for one year generally and three years from the initiating businesses after approval. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Existing-inventory sales rules and pending restocking limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/effective-date notes. Directs enacting rules allowing districts with pending or denied approval requests to sell existing inventory within a reasonable time, while barring restocking or replenishment during a pending request until approval is granted. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised "restocking ban" to "pending restocking limit" to match the statutory rule-of-construction wording during a pending request. (Prior draft: "Rules for selling existing inventory and restocking ban".)

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history/effective-date notes (effective 6-27-00). Authorizes reasonable and necessary rules under chapter 536 (citing section 536.010) and declares section 278.135 and chapter 536 nonseverable, voiding rulemaking authority and rules proposed or adopted after June 27, 2000, if specified general assembly review/disapproval powers are held unconstitutional. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–4 (including subdivisions (1)–(2) and continuation text in sub 2) and history/effective-date notes (effective 6-27-00); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed 3-business-complaint approval trigger, mandatory disclosure of complaint procedure on request, 60-day review/two-part approval criteria/1-year and 3-year complaint bars, existing-inventory sales rules with pending restocking construction limit, and June 27, 2000 chapter 536 nonseverability clause citing section 536.010 (without enforceability claims). Revised subs 1 and 3 titles for completeness and precision; retained subs 2 and 4.

headings.title: District disestablishment petition, referendum, and contract bar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1943 p. 839 § 9, A.L. 1961 p. 31). Requires the state commission upon receiving a disestablishment petition signed by at least 25 land representatives per township to hold a referendum and, upon majority approval, declare the district disestablished, ending supervisors' authority to enter contracts or agreements. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Property disposition, private funds, and two-year reestablishment bar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1943 p. 839 § 9, A.L. 1961 p. 31). Directs the commission after disestablishment to take charge of district property, complete practicable unfinished contracts, sell/transfer property (returning county-funded property to the county commission), return or expend unspent private donations per donor terms, and bar reestablishment under section 278.100 for two years. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (through 1961 p. 31); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed 25-per-township disestablishment petition, majority referendum, post-disestablishment contract bar, property sale/transfer and county-funded property return, private donation handling, and 2-year section 278.100 reestablishment bar. Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Political subdivision status for local government retirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2018 S.B. 892). Classifies a soil and water conservation district organized under sections 278.060 to 278.155 as a political subdivision for sections 70.600 to 70.755 (notwithstanding section 70.600) so employees are eligible for Missouri local government employees' retirement system membership upon the district becoming an "employer" under section 70.600(11). Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised title to remove the unprinted acronym "LAGERS" and reflect the archived statutory reference to the Missouri local government employees' retirement system. (Prior draft: "Political subdivision status for LAGERS retirement eligibility".)

headings.title: Debt and retirement-liability payment check before disestablishment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2018 S.B. 892). Requires the soil and water commission, before declaring a district disestablished under section 278.150, to determine that all outstanding district indebtedness has been paid, including pledged moneys owed to any retirement plan or system for unfunded accrued liability. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 2018 S.B. 892); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed political subdivision status for sections 70.600 to 70.755 (notwithstanding section 70.600) upon becoming a section 70.600(11) employer and mandatory debt/unfunded-retirement-liability payment determination prior to section 278.150 disestablishment. Revised sub 1 title to remove unprinted acronym "LAGERS"; retained sub 2.

headings.title: Subdistrict feasibility determination and public hearing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1957 p. 4 § 278.180, A.L. 1969 S.B. 184). Directs soil and water supervisors to determine whether a proposed subdistrict is desirable, practicable, feasible, and necessary for public health, safety, and general welfare, guarantees interested parties the right to attend and be heard, and allows adjournment for good cause to an announced day certain. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Landowner referendum and sixty-five percent approval threshold
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1957 p. 4 § 278.180, A.L. 1969 S.B. 184). Directs supervisors upon a favorable feasibility finding to conduct a landowner ballot referendum and, if 65% of voting landowners approve, declare the subdistrict duly organized and record the action and official name in official minutes. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (through 1969 S.B. 184); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed subdistrict feasibility/public-welfare determination, interested-party hearing rights, good-cause adjournment to day certain, and 65% voting-landowner referendum threshold with official minutes recording. Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Joint supervisor board for multidistrict watershed districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1957 p. 4 §§ 278.200, 278.210, A.L. 1969 S.B. 184 §§ 278.220, 278.230, A.L. 1977 H.B. 457, A.L. 2001 S.B. 462). Allows filing a multidistrict watershed petition with any affected district's supervisors, requires joint board organization with one-year officers solely for formation, consolidation, expansion, disestablishment, or eminent domain, and grants the same formation manner, powers, and duties as single-district watershed districts. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Certification and recording of watershed district creation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs supervisors, after entering creation in official minutes, to certify the watershed district's creation on a separate form recorded with each affected county's recorder of deeds and the state soil and water districts commission. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (through 2001 S.B. 462); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed joint multidistrict supervisor board limited strictly to formation, consolidation, expansion, disestablishment, or eminent domain with 1-year officers, and separate-form creation certification recorded with county recorders and the state commission. Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Advisory role of soil and water supervisor boards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1957 p. 4 § 278.220, A.L. 1963 p. 407, A.L. 1967 p. 376, A.L. 1969 S.B. 184, A.L. 1977 H.B. 457, A.L. 2001 S.B. 462, A.L. 2005 H.B. 58 merged with H.B. 455). Provides that single or combined boards of soil and water conservation district supervisors act in an advisory capacity to the watershed district board (noting catchline mismatch where the official heading still says "to govern"). Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified catchline-vs-body mismatch: body assigns advisory role to single or combined supervisor boards although official catchline retains "to govern".

headings.title: Watershed trustee election, ballot tax notice, terms, and vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Governs election of five landowner trustees during the establishment referendum (not on regular county political election dates), mandatory ballot notice of a potential tax up to 40 cents per $100 real estate valuation, staggered six-/four-/two-year terms keyed to September 28, 1977, trustee appointment of vacancy successors, reelection, and two-year chairman and secretary terms. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Trustee authority, exclusions, meeting minutes, and expenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes trustees to act in all watershed district matters except formation, consolidation, expansion, or disestablishment, requires the secretary to send meeting minutes to each included soil and water district board, and provides reimbursement for district business expenses (noting official catchline refers narrowly to "mileage reimbursement"). Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised title to explicitly flag the four excluded matters (formation, consolidation, expansion, and disestablishment) alongside trustee governance, minutes, and business expense reimbursement. (Prior draft: "Trustee governance powers, meeting minutes, and expense reimbursement".)

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–3 and history note (through 2005 H.B. 58/H.B. 455); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed major catchline-vs-body mismatches: sub 1 gives soil and water supervisor boards an advisory role (though official catchline says "to govern"), sub 2 governs 5 elected landowner trustees (Sept 28, 1977 staggers, 40-cent ballot tax notice), and sub 3 grants trustees governance except formation/consolidation/expansion/disestablishment plus business expense reimbursement (though catchline says "mileage reimbursement"). Revised sub 3 title to flag governance exclusions explicitly; retained subs 1–2.

headings.title: One-time organization tax levy and authorized uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/footnote notes (L. 1957 p. 4 § 278.230, A.L. 1963 p. 405, A.L. 1967 p. 376, A.L. 1977 H.B. 457, A.L. 1992 S.B. 443, A.L. 2001 S.B. 462). Authorizes watershed trustees to levy a one-time organization tax up to 40 cents per $100 assessed real estate valuation for preliminary work, organization/administration expenses, and property/easement acquisition (retaining archived phrasing omitting a conjunction before "the acquisition") pursuant to subsections 4 and 5. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified archived text omitting a conjunction before "the acquisition" and cross-reference to subsections 4 and 5.

headings.title: Annual improvement tax after sixty-five percent landowner agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source footnote (*Word "the" appears in original rolls, keyed to "the * trustees"). Permits an annual tax pursuant to subsections 4 and 5 for construction, repair, alteration, maintenance, and operation of improvement works to participate in federal watershed protection and flood prevention funds after obtaining conservation agreements and farm plans from owners of at least 65% of district lands. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified original-rolls footnote (*Word "the" appears in original rolls) keyed to "the * trustees" and 65% landowner agreement prerequisite.

headings.title: Annual itemized budget preparation and trustee approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/footnote notes. Requires watershed trustees within the first quarter of each calendar year to prepare an itemized budget for administration and improvement works for the ensuing fiscal year, subject to trustee approval under section 278.240. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Annual levy cap and September 1 county certification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source footnote (*Word "the" appears in original rolls, keyed to "The * trustees"). Directs trustees under section 278.240 to make the necessary real estate levy not exceeding 40 cents per $100 assessed valuation annually and certify the rate to the county commission(s) on or before September 1 for levy with county taxes. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified original-rolls footnote (*Word "the" appears in original rolls) keyed to "The * trustees" and September 1 certification deadline.

headings.title: County tax collection, separate account, and requisition expenditures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history/footnote notes. Directs county taxing/collecting officials to levy and collect watershed taxes with like interest and penalties on regular tax bills and remit collections monthly to the watershed district treasurer for deposit in a separate named account disbursed on requisition of the board chairman and secretary. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Perpetual tax lien on parity with general taxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history/footnote notes. Makes watershed district taxes, interest, default penalties, and collection costs a perpetual lien on parity with general tax liens, not extinguished by any sale to enforce general taxes or other liens. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Delinquent tax sales and county accounting for unsold tracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history/footnote notes. Provides for selling delinquent real property at regular tax sales under general Missouri tax-sale statutes and directs that property receiving no bids be struck off to the county or statutory agency to account to the district like school, town, and city taxes. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Article X, Section 22 and section 137.073 tax status
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history/footnote notes. Deems a watershed ballot tax under section 278.240 approved by voters on or before November 4, 1980, to be the current levy authorized by law on that date for Missouri Constitution Article X, Section 22 purposes even if unimposed or imposed at a lower rate, and treats it as the 1984 tax for section 137.073 if no levy was imposed that year. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified Missouri Constitution Article X, Section 22 (November 4, 1980) and 1984 tax treatment under section 137.073; no enforceability claim added.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–8, history note (through 2001 S.B. 462), and original-rolls footnote (*Word "the" appears in original rolls, keyed to subs 2 and 4); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed one-time 40-cent organization tax (noting omitted conjunction before "the acquisition" in sub 1), 65%-agreement annual improvement tax, Q1 itemized budget, 40-cent cap and Sept 1 certification, monthly county remittances/separate account, parity perpetual lien, delinquent tax sales, and Art. X § 22 (Nov 4, 1980) / section 137.073 (1984) tax treatment without enforceability claims. All 8 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Petitions and procedures for consolidating watershed subdistricts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 184 § 3). Allows filing petitions with soil and water conservation district supervisors to consolidate two or more watershed subdistricts, observing the creation procedures in sections 278.170 to 278.190. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Consolidation referendum threshold and prior bond obligations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 184 § 3). Directs supervisors to declare areas consolidated upon 65% approval of voting landowners in each component area and record the action in official minutes, while keeping taxes for outstanding pre-consolidation bonds solely the obligation of property within the issuing component subdistrict. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 184 § 3); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed consolidation petitions following sections 278.170 to 278.190 procedures, 65% landowner approval in each component area, and proviso keeping pre-consolidation bond taxes solely on property in the issuing component subdistrict. Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: County detachment referendum and prior debt arrangements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2002 S.B. 984 & 985, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1126). Permits a county in an organized watershed subdistrict that has levied the organization tax but not adopted the annual tax under section 278.250 to detach upon majority approval of qualified voters in the county portion, provided trustees first arrange payment of outstanding indebtedness for services or improvements in that county. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Certification and recording of county detachment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2002 S.B. 984 & 985, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1126). Requires watershed district trustees, after recording the county detachment in official minutes, to certify the detachment on a separate form recorded with each affected county's recorder of deeds and the state soil and water districts commission. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (through 2004 H.B. 1126); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed county detachment eligibility (organization tax levied, annual tax under section 278.250 not adopted), majority qualified-voter approval, prior trustee debt-payment arrangements, and separate-form detachment certification recorded with county recorders and the state commission. Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Petitions and procedures for expanding a watershed subdistrict
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 184 § 4). Permits filing petitions with soil and water conservation district supervisors to include additional land in an existing watershed subdistrict, observing the creation procedures of sections 278.170 to 278.190. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Sixty-five percent landowner approval for land inclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 184 § 4). Directs supervisors to declare the proposed area included in the existing subdistrict and record the action in official minutes if 65% of voting landowners in the proposed addition approve in the referendum. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 184 § 4); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed expansion petitions following sections 278.170 to 278.190 procedures and 65% voting-landowner approval in the proposed addition area with minutes recording. Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Financing resolution for general levy or special assessment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/footnote notes (L. 1967 p. 376, A.L. 1972 H.B. 920, A.L. 1977 H.B. 457, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070, A.L. 2001 S.B. 462; footnote *Word "the" appears in original rolls, keyed to "the * trustees"). Directs watershed trustees under section 278.240, upon approval of a plan of work, to propose by resolution financing improvement costs via general levy (subject to section 278.250 limits), special benefit assessment, or a stated combination of both. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified original-rolls footnote (*Word "the" appears in original rolls) keyed to "the * trustees" and section 278.250 general-levy limit reference.

headings.title: Appointment, qualifications, and technical access of three appraisers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/footnote notes. Directs trustees under section 278.240, when special benefit assessment is proposed, to appoint three Missouri-resident appraisers who are not district landowners to recommend benefit apportionment, granting access to engineering data and authority to request additional legal counsel or registered professional engineer data. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Appraisal of property values, benefits, damages, and appraiser pay
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/footnote notes. Directs appraisers to view premises, value property to be acquired within or without the district, assess benefits and damages by tract, railroad right-of-way, and other property, submit written reports to the trustees, and receive payment for services and necessary expenses. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Assessment resolution, notice, hearing, and fixed assessments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source footnote (**Word "or" appears in original rolls, keyed to "board of** trustees"). Directs trustees under section 278.240 to prepare a tract-by-tract assessment resolution capped at estimated benefits, publish complaint-hearing notice under section 278.190, conduct a section 278.200 hearing with power to alter appraisals, and pass a resolution fixing each tract's benefit assessment. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised "final levy" to "fixed assessments" to distinguish fixing tract benefit assessments in subsection 4 from the landowner referendum in subsection 5 and county levy in subsection 6. (Prior draft: "Assessment resolution, published notice, benefit hearing, and final levy".) Verified original-rolls footnote (**Word "or" appears in original rolls) keyed to "board of** trustees" and sections 278.190/278.200 cross-references.

headings.title: Two-thirds landowner referendum on assessments, bonds, and excess levy
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history/footnote notes. Requires trustees under section 278.240 to submit assessed-benefit collection and any proposed bond issue, interest rate, and levy exceeding section 278.250 limits to assessed landowners under sections 278.190 to 278.210 notice and procedure, requiring a two-thirds vote of voting landowners for adoption. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Certification and county levy of general tax and special assessments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history/footnote notes. Directs trustees under section 278.240 to make and certify the general levy rate and special assessment amounts to the county commission(s) for levy alongside county taxes. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Direct bond sales to USDA Rural Development or federal agencies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history/footnote notes. Permits offering section 278.280 bond issues, in whole or part, to USDA Rural Development or another federal agency without public offering or competitive bids. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–7, history note (through 2001 S.B. 462), and both original-rolls footnotes (*Word "the" in sub 1; **Word "or" in sub 4); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed general levy/special assessment financing resolution (section 278.250 limits), 3 Missouri-resident non-landowner appraisers, tract/railroad benefit-damage reports, published notice/hearing/benefit-fixing resolution (sections 278.190/278.200), 2/3 landowner referendum (sections 278.190–278.210), county levy certification, and direct bond sales to USDA Rural Development or federal agencies. Revised sub 4 title from "final levy" to "fixed assessments" to distinguish from subs 5–6; retained subs 1–3 and 5–7.

headings.title: Eligibility, petition, referendum, and debt payment for disestablishment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1967 p. 376, A.L. 1969 S.B. 184, A.L. 2001 S.B. 462). Sets conditions for disestablishing a watershed district organized over five years (no outstanding bonds and either no works/maintenance obligations or approved federal/state/local assumption of O&M), requires a 50% landowner petition and 65% voting-landowner approval under sections 278.190 to 278.210 procedures, and requires paying or arranging payment of outstanding indebtedness before declaring disestablishment. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Certification and recording of watershed district disestablishment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the watershed district supervisors (retaining archived phrase "watershed district supervisors"), after entering disestablishment in official minutes, to certify the fact on a separate form recorded with each affected county's recorder of deeds and the state soil and water districts commission. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified archived phrase "watershed district supervisors" (contrasted with trustees in 278.240 and soil and water conservation district supervisors in subsection 3); retained faithfully.

headings.title: Disposition of disestablished watershed district property and funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs the soil and water conservation district supervisor boards to take charge of disestablished watershed district property and funds, sell property, satisfy obligations, and turn over remaining funds to the respective county commissions. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

All 3 drafted titles retained.
